theater: 珠江流域與五嶺山道（番禺一帶）

battle.name: 秦征百越
battle.theater: 珠江流域與五嶺山道（番禺一帶）
battle.brief: 公元前二一四年，秦始皇三十三年，秦廷在北擊匈奴之後又發兵五十萬戍五嶺，分路深入嶺南。首路主將屠睢兵敗，為越人所射殺，秦軍遂改為據城待機、鑿靈渠通舟楫，趙佗與任囂分守龍州、番禺一線，數年之後平定越地，置南海、桂林、象郡三郡。卡面兵器為埃及月牙劍，此役並無其蹤跡。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 秦征百越是秦朝在統一六國之後對嶺南用兵的一次大規模戰役，時間在秦始皇三十三年，即公元前二一四年，交戰的兩方是關中的秦帝國與活動在長江以南、珠江流域的百越諸部。秦朝一方是標準的中央集權軍國體制：兵源來自全國郡縣按戶籍與兵役制徵發的故秦民、新附之地的民眾，以及一批被徙往嶺南的刑徒，編為步兵、車兵、弩兵與騎兵四種方隊，軍中設將軍、校尉、屯長、什長層級，並有御史與軍吏隨軍監臨；糧秣、器械與徭夫由沿途郡縣供應。這支部隊同時也是工程隊伍，開山、架橋、築城、鑿渠都由同一批人承擔，嶺南的每一次推進都伴隨一次土木工程。百越一方並非單一國家，而是南越、閩越、駱越（西甌）以及更南方的部族聯盟，各部自有首領、兵器與風俗，沒有統一的指揮系統；其共同的戰爭經驗來自春秋末年以來越國舟師水陸兩用的傳統。對秦軍而言，最大障礙不是敵手的兵數，而是五嶺與江南的雨林山嶺、南北不同的氣候與糧道，以及越人熟悉本地水網的舟師。歸根到底，這是一場以國家動員能力對抗地理與分散抵抗的戰爭。
countriesEn: The Qin conquest of Baiyue was a large-scale campaign the Qin state fought in the far south after unifying the six kingdoms, taking place in the thirty-third year of the reign of Qin Shi Huang, that is 214 BC. The two sides were the Qin empire centred on Guanzhong and the peoples of Baiyue who lived south of the Yangtze and along the Pearl River. The Qin side was a textbook centralised military state: the troops were drawn from the populations of the commanderies and counties by the household register and the corvée law, from the newly submitted regions, and from a body of convicts deported to Lingnan; they were organised into four kinds of unit, infantry, chariot troops, crossbowmen and cavalry, with generals, commandants, garrison commanders and squad leaders below them, and surveyors and army scribes riding along to supervise. Grain, weapons and labour were supplied by the commanderies along the route. This was also an engineering army: the same men who cut roads through mountains, bridged rivers, built walls and dug canals carried the advance forward, and every gain in Lingnan was paid for in works of civil engineering. The Baiyue side was not a single state but a league made up of the southern Yue, the Minyue, the Luoyue or Xigu and still more southerly communities, each with its own chiefs, weapons and customs, and with no central command structure; what they shared was a fighting tradition inherited from the Yue state of the late Spring and Autumn period, which fought on water and on land at once. For the Qin army the real obstacle was not the number of enemy troops but the mountains and rainforest of the Five Ridges and of the Jiangnan, the difference in climate between north and south, the grain route, and the war boats of a people who knew the local waterways intimately. In the end this was a war of state mobilisation against geography and dispersed resistance.
people: 決定這場戰爭的人首先是秦始皇嬴政。統一只用了十年，他隨即把新王朝的兵鋒推向四面：前二一五年蒙恬領三十萬眾北擊匈奴，取河南地，隔了一年南面再舉，前二一四年發兵五十萬戍五嶺。兩役相接，兵源、財力與民力都出自同一批郡縣，北疆還要留兵守塞、築直道，這一取捨後世多有非議。廷中有魏國來客尉繚，據《史記》所載，他論用兵以詐立、以利動、以分合為變，主張審時度勢、避實擊虛，認為天下初定、民力未復，北伐與南征不宜同時大舉；秦始皇聽不進，傳記說他因此怒而遣走尉繚。真正帶兵入嶺南的是屠睢、趙佗、任囂三位將軍。屠睢是首路主將，銳進深入，兵敗被越人乘夜襲營所射殺，這一挫折直接改變了全役打法。屠睢既死，趙佗與任囂收拾局面，任囂為南海尉，趙佗屯兵龍州一帶，築城置守，開山越之道；任囂先卒，趙佗代領南海尉，主政嶺南，越人此後只能與秦廷的郡縣官吏打交道。越人那邊，《史記》與《越絕書》一類文獻沒有留下領兵者的名字，只留下「越人習水，善舟師」與「水行而山處，以船為車，以楫為馬」一類群體描述，這種不留名的抵抗方式本身就是秦軍最難破解的對手。
peopleEn: The man who decided this war was Qin Shi Huang, Ying Zheng. He had needed only ten years to unify the empire, and he immediately turned the arms of the new dynasty in every direction: in 215 BC Meng Tian took three hundred thousand men north against the Xiongnu and seized the territory south of the Yellow River; a year later the south was raised in turn, and in 214 BC the court sent five hundred thousand men to garrison the Five Ridges. The two campaigns ran back to back, drawing troops, money and labour from the same commanderies, while the northern front still had to be held and walled, and later writers have often criticised that choice. In the court there was Wei Liao, who had come from the state of Wei. The Shiji records him arguing that war must rest on deception, on advantage and on shifting and combining the formation, and that the times had to be weighed: the realm had only just been unified and the people were worn out, so a great northern expedition and a great southern one should not be launched at once. The first emperor would not hear it, and the tradition says he was angry and sent Wei Liao away. The men who actually led the army into Lingnan were three generals: Tu Sui, Zhao Tuo and Ren Xiao. Tu Sui commanded the first column, pressed forward too fast, and was killed when the Yue struck his camp at night; that blow changed the character of the whole campaign. With Tu Sui dead, Zhao Tuo and Ren Xiao took stock of the situation, Ren Xiao became the commandant of Nanhai while Zhao Tuo based himself with his column around Longzhou, building and holding towns and opening the mountain roads of the Yue. Ren Xiao died first, and Zhao Tuo succeeded him as commandant of Nanhai and took charge of Lingnan; from then on the Yue could deal with no one but the officials and clerks of the Qin commanderies. On the Yue side neither the Shiji nor the Yuejue Shu preserves the name of a single commander, only collective descriptions such as the Yue being at home on the water and skilled with boats, travelling over the mountains as they travelled over the water, using the boat as a carriage and the oar as a horse. That anonymity is itself the hardest of adversaries for the Qin army to overcome.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍出自古埃及的中王國時代，形制是外彎的單刃格殺器，年代比本役早一千兩百餘年。它的刃線是從更早的鐮形工具與所謂鴨嘴斧一脈演化而來，砍擊時靠弧度把力量帶進目標，不似直刃劍那樣需要拔出再砍，屬於早期金屬時代的近身格殺技術。嶺南戰場上不可能出現月牙劍一類兵器，更不可能有持月牙劍的隊伍，它只能作為同時代另一個大陸的技術對照來讀。真正在場的兵器分屬兩個技術圈。秦軍以弩為主力遠程殺傷手段，銅弩機已能模組化生產，湖北江陵睡虎地秦墓與陝西臨潼一帶出土的弩機可以印證；近身用戈、矛、戟與劍，劍作圓莖，有環首或盤首，護身有皮甲與札甲，車兵用雙輪戎車，御者自駕一馬或二馬。越人的兵器形制不同，兩廣越人墓葬出土的直身有格銅劍，格上飾菱形暗格紋，圓首無柄，與中原秦劍分屬兩個傳統；此外有銅矛、銅戈、竹木削成的長槍與弓矢，藤牌與皮盾用於林地。攻城與運輸方面，秦軍有《墨子·公輸篇》所記的鈎梯、飛樓、穴車一類器械，牛車、徭夫隊與新造舟船，番禺一帶的船場與冶銅作場是全役的支撐。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Egyptian khopesh, a single-edged, outward-curving chopping sword of the Middle Kingdom period, roughly twelve hundred and eighty years older than this campaign. Its cutting curve descends from older sickle forms and from the so-called duckbill axe, and the swing of the blade carries the force into the target without the need to pull the weapon free and strike again; it belongs to the close-quarters technology of the early metal ages. Nothing of that kind could have stood on a battlefield in Lingnan, and there was certainly no body of troops carrying khopeshes; the card can only be read as a technical comparison drawn from another continent of the same broad period. The weapons actually present belonged to two different technical circles. The Qin army relied on the crossbow as its principal long-range arm: bronze trigger mechanisms were already being produced in series, as the crossbow mechanisms excavated from the Qin tombs at Shuihudi in Jiangling, Hubei, and around Lintong in Shaanxi attest. At close quarters they carried ge, mao, ji and jian, the swords having a round tang and a ring or disc pommel; they wore leather and lamellar armour, and their chariot troops used two-wheeled war wagons driven by one or two horses. The weapons of the Yue were of a different shape. The straight swords with a guard recovered from Yue burials in the Two Guangs carry lozenge-shaped fluting in dark relief upon the guard, a round pommel and no handle proper, and they belong to a tradition entirely distinct from the swords of the Qin. Alongside them the Yue had bronze mao and ge, spears of bamboo and wood hardened and sharpened, bows and arrows, and rattan or hide shields for the forest fighting. For siege and transport the Qin brought devices of the kind described in the Gongsheng chapter of the Mohzi, hook-ladders, flying towers and burrowing carts, together with ox carts, labour gangs and newly built boats; the shipyards and the bronze foundry at Panyu supported the whole operation.
tactics: 秦軍的整套打法可以分三段。第一段是進攻。五十萬人不可能一次投入同一條路，史料可見秦軍分路：一路沿湘江谷地南下，取湘南與桂北的越人據點；一路自江西、廣東方向沿海北上，逼近珠江口；一路負責攻取江浙閩地。每一路都配備兩種力量，一種能打，一種能修路，攻城之前先由工兵砍出通道、在渡口架橋、在要衝築城。秦軍的射擊以弩為主，弩機可瞄準、可重複使用，射速雖低，射程與精度都勝過越人的弓；步兵以盾與戈矛結陣前進，車兵在前列橫陳，用來突破越人依山傍水的狹隘陣地。越人的應對是避實擊虛：不與秦軍在開闊地硬拼，退入山嶺、洞穴與雨林，等待秦軍隊形被山道拉長、糧隊與舟隊拉開，再以小股兵力夜襲營寨，射殺主將，焚擾糧道。第一段最重的一擊正出在這裡，屠睢所部深入後遭夜襲，主將陣亡，秦軍一度氣沮。第二段轉為據守與工程。趙佗、任囂不再求速，改在龍州、番禺一線築城固守，並在湘水與漓水之間開鑿靈渠，使糧秣與器械可由水路直達嶺南，把嶺北的粟米與中原的鐵器換成前線的食糧與兵械。越人則以舟師在珠江水系出沒，襲擾秦軍的糧船與巡道船，秦軍以弩陣加舟師沿岸掃蕩，切斷水陸聯絡。嶺南自四月至九月為雨季，山道崩塌、河水暴漲，秦軍屢受其阻，軍中又多有疫病，士卒減員與糧秣腐敗是這一役最難解決的兩個問題。第三段是分化與收編。越部之間並不團結，秦廷一面用郡縣、爵位與安置移民的手段拉攏歸附的部首領，一面對仍在抵抗者用兵，兩手並用，嶺南的抵抗由整體轉為零散，最後以設郡編戶收束。
tacticsEn: The whole method of the Qin army can be divided into three stages. The first was the advance. Five hundred thousand men could not be committed to a single road, and the records show the army moving in separate columns: one down the valley of the Xiang River against the Yue strongholds of southern Hunan and northern Guangxi, one advancing northward by sea from the Jiangxi and Guangdong directions to close on the mouth of the Pearl River, and one assigned to the reduction of the Jiangnan and the Minyue lands. Each column carried two kinds of force, one able to fight and one able to build, and before any siege the engineers cut a road, bridged the crossings and raised a fort on the line of advance. Qin shooting was built on the crossbow: the mechanism could be aimed and used again and again, slow to reload but superior in range and accuracy to the bows of the Yue; infantry advanced in closed order with shields, ge and mao, while chariot troops deployed in front to break the narrow positions the Yue held beside hills and water. The Yue answered by refusing to give ground in the open: they withdrew into mountains, caves and rainforest, waited for the Qin columns to be stretched out along the mountain roads and the baggage and boat trains to be pulled apart, and then struck the camps at night with small parties, killing commanders, burning and worrying the grain route. The heaviest blow of this stage fell exactly there: Tu Sui's column, deep in the mountains, was attacked at night and its commander killed, and the Qin army lost heart for a time. The second stage was a turn towards holding ground and engineering. Zhao Tuo and Ren Xiao gave up the attempt to finish quickly, built and held towns along the line of Longzhou and Panyu, and cut the Lingqu canal between the Xiang and the Li so that grain and equipment could reach Lingnan by water, turning the millet of the northern hills and the iron of the central plain into rations and weapons at the front. The Yue meanwhile put their war boats into the Pearl River system to harass Qin grain boats and river patrols, and the Qin answered with crossbow formations and river squadrons sweeping the banks to cut the water and land communications. In Lingnan the rainy season ran from the fourth to the ninth month; mountain tracks collapsed and rivers ran high, repeatedly blocking the Qin, and sickness thinned the army as well, so that the two hardest problems of the campaign were the falling away of soldiers and the spoiling of grain. The third stage was division and enrolment. The Yue communities were not united with one another, so the court worked with two hands at once, drawing in the chiefs who were willing to submit by offering commanderies, ranks and settlement for the displaced, and continuing to fight those who still resisted. Resistance in Lingnan thus passed from a general rising to scattered episodes, and was finally closed off by the establishment of commanderies and the registration of households.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。兵員方面，《史記·秦始皇本紀》記秦始皇三十三年「發兵五十萬，戍五嶺」，《史記·南越列傳》又記秦廷在略取陸梁之地後徙民戍嶺南，兩處都出現五十萬這個數，歷來學者多以為二者或是同一批人力的兩種說法，或互相重疊，不宜當作兩支各五十萬的部隊相加；五十萬是史書明載的概數，包含沿途屯戍與轉輸所需的人力，真正投入戰鬥的當然只是其中一部分。同一時期蒙恬北擊匈奴記三十萬，兩役相接，數字之間亦難免互相借用。統制方面，嶺南之役由屠睢、趙佗、任囂三將分道，主將屠睢陣亡。設治方面，秦平越後置南海、桂林、象郡三郡，南海郡治番禺，桂林郡治布山，象郡治臨塵，郡縣官吏的任命自此役開始。工程方面，靈渠連接湘水與漓水，人工開鑿段約三十餘公里，由監御史祿主持，事關全役的糧運；五嶺指越城、都龐、萌渚、駱越、大庾一線山地，通道的開鑿決定了推進速度。時間方面，出師在公元前二一四年，嶺南的抵抗延續數年，秦亡於前二〇六年，趙佗於前二〇四年自立為南越王，前一一一年漢武帝平南越，自秦發兵到南越覆亡，前後約一百零三年。本役出師的月份史書沒有明文，只記「發兵五十萬，戍五嶺」，本卡所標月份係按秦軍於秋後出師、翌年雨季前抵達嶺南的通說取八月，並非史書記載。傷亡數字史無明文，不能編造。
dataEn: The numbers that can be written down with grounds are roughly these. On troops, the Shiji has it that in the thirty-third year of Qin Shi Huang five hundred thousand men were sent to garrison the Five Ridges, and the Shiji chapter on Nanyue records that after taking the land of Luliang the court deported people to garrison Lingnan; the figure of five hundred thousand appears in both places, and scholars have long held that the two are either two descriptions of the same body of men or overlap each other, and that they should not be added together as two armies of five hundred thousand apiece. Five hundred thousand is an explicit figure in the historical record, but it is a summary number, and it includes the men needed for garrisoning the line and for transport; only a part of it was ever committed to battle. The thirty thousand hundred men recorded for Meng Tian's northern campaign against the Xiongnu belong to the same period, and the two sets of figures can hardly avoid borrowing from one another. On command, the Lingnan war was divided among three generals, Tu Sui, Zhao Tuo and Ren Xiao, and the first of them was killed in action. On administration, after the Yue were pacified the Qin set up the three commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang, with the seat of Nanhai at Panyu, that of Guilin at Bushan and that of Xiang at Linchen; the appointment of the first commandery officials dates from this campaign. On works, the Lingqu canal joined the Xiang and the Li, its hand-dug section running for some thirty kilometres or more, and it was directed by the censor-in-chief Lu; the fate of the whole campaign hung on it as a grain route. The Five Ridges are the line of mountains running through Yucheng, Dugang, Mengzhu, Luoyue and Dayu, and the speed of the advance was decided by the roads cut through them. On time, the army set out in 214 BC, resistance in Lingnan ran on for several years, the Qin fell in 206 BC, Zhao Tuo assumed the title of king of Nanyue in 204 BC, and in 111 BC the campaigns of Emperor Wu of Han destroyed Nanyue; from the Qin dispatch to the fall of Nanyue is about a hundred and three years. The month in which the army set out is not given in the records, which say only that five hundred thousand men were sent to garrison the Five Ridges; the month shown on this card follows the general view that the Qin marched out after the autumn harvest and reached Lingnan before the rains of the following year, and it is not a date taken from the sources. There is no record of losses, and none can be invented.
cause: 打這場仗的起因，是秦朝要在統一之後把「天下」變成真正可以治理的天下。前二二一年滅齊、統一度量衡與文字、築長城、修直道之後，秦廷手上有的是制度，缺的是嶺南：珠江流域的越地從未入郡縣，貢賦不上，道路不通，中原的命令走到五嶺為止就散在雨林與山峽裡。秦始皇要的並非一場征服，而是把越地變成可以收稅、可以徵兵、可以調度的郡縣，這就要求先打通通道，再設郡置吏。工程上的目標與軍事上的目標在這裡重疊：靈渠的開鑿不是為了好看，而是要把湘江的水運接到漓江，把關中與中原的糧秣、器械和刑徒一口氣送到嶺南，再從番禺分送各處。北方也在拉緊：前二一五年蒙恬已取河南地，匈奴退往幕北，秦廷需要一段沒有北面牽制的時間來辦南面的事。內部曾有反對意見，尉繚一類人物主張天下初定、民力未復，連年徵發與同時用兵會把剛剛建立起來的秩序拖垮，記錄說秦始皇沒有採納。結果是南北兩面同時抽走同一批人力與糧秣：北疆留兵守塞、築直道，南面再發五十萬眾，五嶺的雨季與瘴癘又讓這支部隊遲遲無法速決。越人方面的抵抗並非出於統一，而是出於各自的土地、宗族與水路利益，秦廷若不能先解決通道與糧道，郡縣的紙面命令就落不到地上。
causeEn: The reason this war was fought is that the Qin wanted, after unification, to turn the realm into something that could actually be governed. After the defeat of Qi in 221 BC, the unification of the weights and measures and of the script, the building of the Great Wall and the cutting of the straight road, the court had plenty of institutions and lacked only Lingnan: the Yue country of the Pearl River had never entered a commandery, its tribute did not come, its roads did not connect, and an order from the central plain dispersed into the rainforest and the gorges as soon as it reached the Five Ridges. What Qin Shi Huang wanted was not a conquest but a territory that could be taxed, levied and redirected, and that meant opening the routes first and then appointing officials and setting up commanderies. Here the engineering aim and the military aim overlapped: the Lingqu canal was not cut for show, but to link the water transport of the Xiang to that of the Li, so that the grain, the weapons and the convicts of Guanzhong and the central plain could be carried into Lingnan in one movement and then distributed from Panyu. The north was tightening as well: in 215 BC Meng Tian had already taken the land south of the Yellow River and the Xiongnu had withdrawn north of the desert, and the court needed a stretch of time free of pressure in the north to conduct the business of the south. There was dissent inside the court. Men of the kind of Wei Liao held that the realm had only just been unified and the people were exhausted, that repeated levies and wars on two fronts together would drag down the order that had just been created; the records say the first emperor did not accept it. In the result the two fronts drew on the same men and the same grain at the same time: the north was held by garrisons and by the works of the straight road, the south was given another five hundred thousand men, and the rains and the miasma of the Five Ridges kept that army from finishing its business. On the Yue side the resistance was not a matter of opposing unification as such; it was a matter of land, of lineages and of the rights of the waterways, and until the Qin solved the roads and the grain route, the written orders of the commanderies could not be made to reach the ground.
impact: 這場戰爭最深遠的影響，是嶺南第一次被編入中原王朝的郡縣體系。秦平越後置南海、桂林、象郡三郡，官吏、律令、度量衡與車同軌的做法逐步推到珠江流域，靈渠與湘江水路成為嶺北與嶺南之間長期使用的交通骨幹，番禺由軍事的轉運點變成嶺南的首府與造船冶銅之地。越人並沒有因此消失，而是從獨立的部族變成編戶齊民的新編民，與北來移民在往後數代裡混居融合，中原的姓氏、器物與信仰在珠江水系傳開，嶺南的語言、舟船與風俗也留在郡縣社會裡，成為漢代嶺南的基本面貌。制度上的傳承是雙向的：漢承秦制，郡縣、律令、徭役、屯田與以刑徒實邊的做法一併被漢朝接下來，漢武帝平南越之後設交趾刺史部，交趾、南海、蒼梧三郡的建置幾乎是前二一四年那一役的翻版。另一面的代價極為沉重：五十萬眾與第二批徙民同屯嶺南，糧秣運不上，疫病與雨季造成大量減員，秦朝的民力與財政被拉成一根繃緊的弦。賈誼《過秦論》批評秦「躡足行伍」、不恤民力，正是指着這類連年徵發而言；公元前二一〇年秦始皇死，二世即位而天下已亂，陳勝吳廣起義，前二〇六年秦亡，嶺南秩序隨之崩解。趙佗帶着秦朝的官署與印信自立，前二〇四年稱南越武王，中原與嶺南的統一中斷了九十餘年，直到前一一一年漢武帝用兵才恢復。兵器史上的收穫也實在：銅弩機的大量配發是世界早期金屬弩大規模投入戰爭的案例之一，嶺南出土的兩廣越人墓葬兵器顯示本地原有的格紋銅劍傳統與中原直身劍在此後逐步合流，而廣西合浦與越南清化出土的漢墓銅鼓與雙體船飾件，記下了秦漢水軍在珠江與紅河兩條水系上的實際活動。
impactEn: The deepest effect of this war was that Lingnan was drawn for the first time into the commandery system of a central Chinese dynasty. After the Yue were pacified the Qin set up the three commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang, and the practices of the officials, the statutes and ordinances, the weights and measures and the uniform gauge of the roads were carried step by step into the basin of the Pearl River. The Lingqu canal and the waterway of the Xiang became the standing backbone of traffic between the hills north of the range and the country south of it, and Panyu changed from a military transhipment point into the capital of Lingnan and a place of shipbuilding and bronze casting. The Yue did not thereby disappear: they passed from independent communities into registered households, and in the generations that followed they lived side by side and mingled with settlers from the north. Surnames, objects and beliefs of the central plain spread along the watercourses of the Pearl River, while the speech, the boats and the customs of Lingnan remained inside the commandery society and became the basic face of Han-era Lingnan. The inheritance of institutions ran both ways. The Han took over the Qin forms, and the commanderies, the statutes, the corvée, the garrison farms and the practice of settling the frontier with convicts were all carried on. After Emperor Wu of Han destroyed Nanyue he set up the inspectorate of Jiaoji, and the three commanderies of Jiaoji, Nanhai and Cangwu were very nearly a repetition of the campaign of 214 BC. The cost on the other side was heavy. Five hundred thousand men and a second batch of deportees were stationed in Lingnan together; the grain could not be brought up, sickness and the rainy season thinned the ranks, and the manpower and the finances of the Qin were drawn to a taut string. When Jia Yi blamed the Qin in his essay on the faults of the Qin for making the people march to the ranks and never sparing their strength, he was pointing at levies of this kind. Qin Shi Huang died in 210 BC, his successor took the throne into an empire already in disorder, the rising of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang followed, and in 206 BC the Qin fell, taking the order of Lingnan with it. Zhao Tuo carried the offices and the seals of the Qin with him and ruled on his own, calling himself King Wu of Nanyue in 204 BC; the unity of the central plain and Lingnan was interrupted for more than ninety years and was only restored by the campaigns of Emperor Wu in 111 BC. The gains in the history of weapons are real as well. The mass issue of bronze crossbow mechanisms is one of the clearest cases of a metal crossbow being put into war on a large scale in the early world, and the weapons from Yue burials in the Two Guangs show that the local tradition of the fluted bronze sword and the straight sword of the central plain gradually merged afterwards. The bronze drums and the fittings of a two-hulled boat found in Han tombs at Hepu in Guangxi and in Thanh Hoa in Vietnam record the actual activity of Qin and Han river squadrons on the two water systems of the Pearl River and the Red River.
result: 就公元前二一四年這場戰爭而言，結果是秦軍以國家動員的體量換到了嶺南：出師之後先折一將，屠睢所部深入嶺地，為越人乘夜襲營所射殺，秦軍一度氣沮，趙佗、任囂接手，改以據城、修路、開渠待機為主，不再求戰速；越人的抵抗此後化為零散的游擊與舟師擾斷，秦廷一面用郡縣與安置移民的辦法分化各部，一面逐個擊破，數年之後嶺南大致平定，三郡建置，番禺成為嶺南的軍政與轉運中心。如果只看軍事，這是一場秦廷完勝、對手沒有留下可查名字的戰爭；代價是五十萬眾與第二批徙民陷在雨林與瘴癘之間，北疆同時留著三十萬人，兩個戰場的消耗疊在一起，成為秦朝速亡的重要背景。秦亡之後趙佗沒有散掉這套機器，他承用秦朝的郡縣與官署，帶着秦人將吏與銅印，前二〇四年自立為南越武王，前一一一年才被漢武帝所平，南越立國九十餘年，比秦朝本身長。真正的結局因此落在漢武帝手上，同一片土地，同一套郡縣，最後由漢朝收編。反過來看卡面這件兵器：埃及月牙劍屬於青銅時代早期那種外彎單刃、砍下去不用拔的格殺器，嶺南戰場上真正用來格殺的是秦軍的圓莖環首銅劍與越人的直身有格銅劍，刃線與握法都已是另一個時代；一把早了一千二百餘年的弧刃短器留在卡面上，倒像是提醒人：同一場戰爭裡的兵器，總是站在各自技術世代的末端。
resultEn: As for the war of 214 BC itself, the result was that the Qin bought Lingnan with the weight of its state mobilisation. The army set out and at once lost a general: Tu Sui's column, driven deep into the hills, was shot down by Yue who attacked the camp at night, and for a time the Qin army lost heart. Zhao Tuo and Ren Xiao took over and turned to holding towns, cutting roads and digging canals, waiting rather than hurrying; the resistance of the Yue thereafter broke into scattered raids and war-boat harassment, and the court worked at once to divide the various communities by commanderies and settlement, and to break them one by one. A few years later Lingnan was broadly pacified, the three commanderies were established, and Panyu became the military, administrative and transport centre of the south. Judged purely as a military affair this was a complete victory for the Qin court, over an enemy that left behind no name that can be looked up. The price was paid by the five hundred thousand men and the second batch of deportees trapped between rainforest and miasma, while three hundred thousand men were still held in the north; the consumption of two theatres lay on top of one another and became one of the great background causes of the swift fall of the Qin. When the Qin perished, Zhao Tuo did not let the machine fall apart: he kept the commanderies and the offices of the Qin, the Qin clerks and the Qin seals, and in 204 BC raised the title of King Wu of Nanyue. Nanyue was destroyed only in 111 BC by Emperor Wu of Han, so that the kingdom lasted for more than ninety years, longer than the Qin themselves. The true conclusion therefore belongs to Emperor Wu: the same land, the same commanderies, in the end taken over by the Han. Looked at from the other side, at the weapon on the card: the Egyptian khopesh belongs to that early metal age in which a single outward-curved blade struck and did not need to be pulled back, while the blades actually used to kill in Lingnan were the round-tanged ring-pommelled bronze swords of the Qin and the straight guarded bronze swords of the Yue, whose edge line and grip belong to a different age. A short curved weapon a thousand two hundred and eighty years earlier left sitting on the card is almost a reminder that the weapons in any single war always stand at the end of their own generation of technique.
